name: Calanais (Callanish) Standing Stones, Calanais I
about: Calanais I on the west coast of Lewis: a flattened ring of 13 Lewisian gneiss stones round a central monolith about 4.8 m tall, with a north-north-east avenue of two rows (19 stones), short rows to the east, south and west, two outliers (Stones 9 and 34) and Stone 35 south-east of the ring, and a small chambered cairn squeezed between the monolith and the east side of the ring; 49 stones stand. The monolith and ring were set up around 2900 BC or a little before (Ashmore prefers 2950-2850 BC), the cairn after about 2500 BC; the rows may be later (the innermost east-row stone 2560-1690 cal BC). Peat about 1.5 m deep buried the lower parts from the 1st millennium BC until it was cleared in 1857 on Sir James Matheson's orders. Restored: Stone 35 set up after 1857 (by 1867) and set in concrete; Stone 33a, found fallen in the peat in 1977, re-erected in its own socket on 20 July 1982; the tip of Stone 19 put back in 1978; parts of the cairn rebuilt after 1857 and again after the 1980-81 excavations; some stones have cement patches. Stone numbers follow Somerville (1912) as used by Ashmore (2016): 1-8 and 34 east side of the avenue, 10-19 west side, 20-23 west row, 24-28 south row (24 southernmost), 29 central monolith, 30-33 and 33a east row (30 innermost), 9 and 35 outliers, 41-53 the ring (43 and 44 flank the cairn passage). Research file for the 3D model; quotes are exact text from the cited pages (whitespace normalised); 'derived' marks values computed or inferred.

gaps: Heights of individual stones are not published as text: Ashmore's Illus 3.6 and 24.76 graph the avenue heights from Pitt-Rivers' 1885 record and his Table data are graphical only; the Pontings' 'Callanish: the Documentary Record' (1979) and Curtis and Curtis (2008) probably list them but are not online. Only Stone 29 (4.75-4.8 m), Stone 19 (11 ft 10 in), Stone 12 (1.14 m), Stone 33a (2.77 m long) and the ring average (3 m, up to 3.5 m) are sourced.

Canmore (site 4156; I tried 4108) and trove.scot refuse scripts (HTTP 403), as do the HES property page with the project's user agent, calanais.org (403) and callanishstones.co.uk (Curtis); none of their text is used.

The 'Sleeping Beauty' is identified by the Setting Document only as the range to the south-east; no fetchable source here names it as the Pairc hills (the Setting Document mentions 'the hills of Pairc and Uig' among the views). Isle of Albion wrongly puts it at Clisham.
Ruggles' own text (Astronomy in Prehistoric Britain and Ireland, 1999, pp. 134-136, 159) is not online; his view is quoted through Ashmore.

No azimuths or horizon altitudes for the avenue or rows were found in a fetchable source (Somerville's 1912 figures are summarised but not given by Ashmore); bidb.sky_horizon can compute the skyline and moon path for the model.
Stone shapes in plan: the OSM outlines are uniform placeholders; real outlines need the Glasgow plan (not openly licensed) or Somerville's 1912 plan (out of copyright, scan not located).
Callanish II and III figures disagree between Wikipedia and Ashmore/Ponting; Ashmore's figures (from Ponting and Ponting 2000) are the more authoritative.
